Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

UtilsR 0.6.8

  • fmt_boxplot() resolves complete vertical or horizontal summary mappings automatically for independent identity-statistic overlays, retaining source groups and deferred data callbacks while leaving explicit mappings unchanged.

  • fmt_boxplot() retains explicit NULL controls, including width and alpha, instead of replacing them with wrapper defaults. Omitted controls retain their existing defaults and explicit values follow native validation.

  • fmt_boxplot() copies raw positions from staged source mappings while omitting computed-statistic and after-scale positions in independent overlays. Explicit boxplot mappings keep their evaluation stages and environments.

  • fmt_point() retains missing character shapes during white-border normalization instead of failing before ggplot2 handles missing points.

  • fmt_point() samples indices before slicing matrix-column data, avoiding full-data group copies while retaining native binding and matrix attributes.

  • fmt_point() samples joint discrete colour/fill strata and existing facets; explicit groups retain priority, and layers missing facet columns still replicate.

  • fmt_point() respects explicit point/jitter positions supplied through ..., including position objects and native position names.

  • fmt_point() diagnoses fixed aesthetic vectors and external row-vector mappings before sampling, with instructions to map columns in layer data.

  • fmt_point() uses exact parameter lookups, preventing ignored geom arguments from partially matching inheritance, shape, colour or fill controls.

  • fmt_point() resolves dodge groups from built layer data, so continuous or NULL aesthetics retain plain jitter widths and data callbacks remain deferred.

  • fmt_point() supports group-only jitter-dodge on ggplot2 3.5.x without adding visible aesthetics or changing ggplot2 4.x positioning.

  • fmt_point() samples rows independently of hidden dplyr grouping attributes; rowwise and grouped inputs follow the same aesthetic-based sample limits.

  • fmt_point() distinguishes ordinary columns named stage, after_stat, after_scale or from_theme from delayed aesthetic function calls.

  • fmt_point(white_border = TRUE) keeps non-fillable symbols visible using a white underlay, and handles named shapes and an explicit NULL shape.

  • fmt_point() uses the raw start expression of staged aesthetics for stratified sampling while retaining later colour transformations.

  • fmt_point() samples row indices before slicing grouped data, reducing copying while preserving row order and random selections. Matrix columns retain the existing path; single-column data frames keep their dimensions.

  • fmt_point() validates sample sizes, seeds and layout controls consistently, rejects malformed jitter options and incompatible grouping lengths, and accepts NULL jitter dimensions for ggplot2’s native defaults.

  • fmt_point() forwards supported beeswarm.args options such as priority and side, and rejects unknown, duplicate or unnamed options.

  • fmt_point() includes explicit and layer-local groups in automatic dodging and ignores parent mappings when inherit.aes = FALSE.

  • fmt_point() respects layer-local mappings and inherit.aes when sampling and styling points. Explicit shape/size values override mappings, while omitted values retain the mapped aesthetics.

  • fmt_point() supports sampling function/formula data after the callback runs at build time. Sampling callbacks do not capture unrelated plots or data.

  • fmt_point(white_border = TRUE) retains scaled group colours and existing fills, treats color and colour consistently, and supports mapped shapes and shape 25 without replacing the original plot’s scales.

  • fmt_point() adds independent point layers to every nested patchwork leaf while preserving layout, annotations, spacers and the original plots.

  • fmt_point() samples expression-based groups, retains missing groups, and prioritizes explicit groups over discrete colour/fill mappings. Continuous colour/fill values no longer create one sampling group per distinct value.

  • fmt_point() preserves the caller’s random-number state when sampling, including calls that keep all rows and sessions without an existing seed.

  • check_na() and lv() count a special value (“unknown”, “blank”, “n/a”, “na”, “missing”, “unspecified”, “not available” or an empty string) only as a whole word and once per value. “Regional”, “Canada”, “anaplastic” or “NACT” no longer count through “na”, and “Unknown/unstaged/unspecified” counts once instead of twice. Matching runs on the distinct values, which makes check_na() about ten times and lv() about a third faster on a 257,000-row SEER table.

  • fmt_ref() keeps batching with scalar na.rm and lineend arguments while retaining native rendering, missing-value warnings and fallback for other args.

  • fmt_ref() creates separate reference layers for each subplot, so subsequent edits to one subplot’s reference data or styles do not alter its peers.

  • fmt_ref() uses native per-line layers when facet expressions reference its helper-column prefix, preserving panels without evaluating data callbacks.

  • fmt_ref() constructs self-contained reference mappings and layers, avoiding retention of peer plots and their data when a formatted subplot is extracted.

  • fmt_ref() uses factor color labels consistently in batched and native layers, preserving numeric palette indices, missing colors and encoded transparency.

  • Dedicated fmt_ref() regression tests cover native rendering, transformed and non-numeric positions, nested containers, input preservation and deferred data.

  • fmt_ref() gives argument-specific errors for empty and non-vector line styles when positions are supplied. Unused styles, native missing-value semantics, date positions and discrete category labels are retained.

  • fmt_ref() rejects colour with a suggestion to use its color parameter, avoiding duplicate aesthetics and silently ignored colour requests.

  • fmt_ref() batches reference lines by direction, retaining per-line styles, facet replication and existing colour scales. Other geom arguments keep the native per-line path for compatibility.

  • fmt_ref() rejects geom intercept argument names with a clear suggestion to use x and y. The formatting vignette now uses those supported arguments.

  • fmt_boxplot() aligns independent overlays with scalar fixed source x or y positions by mapping those constants before computing statistics. Explicit boxplot positions and cleared mappings retain priority; fixed vectors are not copied and data callbacks remain deferred.

  • fmt_boxplot() tries range-only blank layers after ordinary sample layers, retaining blank-only sources and documenting explicit source selection when point annotations share a plot with sample points.

  • fmt_boxplot() supports independent vector mappings without an explicit data frame while retaining their environments and deferred evaluation.

  • fmt_boxplot() retains the first single-axis source instead of replacing it with later two-axis layers in independent overlays.

  • fmt_boxplot() preserves the mapping-source order when explicit data are supplied, avoiding unused parent columns in independent overlays.

  • fmt_boxplot() matches data, mapping and stat argument names exactly, preventing unrecognized names from changing samples or statistics while retaining native geom validation and warnings.

  • fmt_boxplot() preserves explicit summary mappings for identity statistics, supporting vertical and horizontal precomputed boxplots without injecting unrelated raw-data axes. Data callbacks remain deferred.

  • fmt_boxplot() selects data and position mappings actually used by existing layers before unused parent settings, avoiding incompatible or empty parent samples. Automatic empty data frames are skipped; explicit empty data and deferred callbacks retain their normal behaviour.

  • fmt_boxplot() skips text, label, segment, curve and reference-line layers when selecting samples automatically, preserving valid single-axis sources instead of replacing them with annotation coordinates.

  • fmt_boxplot() preserves explicitly cleared x or y mappings in independent overlays, including cleared mappings inherited from an existing source layer.

  • fmt_boxplot() rejects malformed argument lists, invalid inheritance flags, non-aesthetic mappings and non-plot gg components with clear input errors.

  • fmt_boxplot() honours explicitly supplied outlier shapes, including NULL, while retaining hidden outlier markers as the default.

  • fmt_boxplot() formats every leaf of nested patchworks while preserving layouts, annotations, plot-list names and non-plot placeholders or overlays.

  • fmt_boxplot() resolves independent overlays from existing layer data and position mappings, preserving deferred evaluation and single-axis boxplots. Missing sources now give a clear error instead of enabling inheritance.

  • fmt_boxplot() retains explicit data, mappings and deferred data callbacks in independent layers, filling only missing position mappings from the plot.

  • fmt_panel() lets restored grid placeholders inherit blank parent-grid settings during and after formatting, preserving explicit blank-inheritance overrides and the restoration of grids hidden by a blank root line.

  • fmt_panel() gives automatically restored grids contrasting colours when a blank root line hides them, including on dark panels with theme_void(), while preserving explicit colours and transparent backgrounds.

  • fmt_panel() retains empty themes in its batch cache on older ggplot2 versions, keeping batch grid output identical to formatting plots individually.

  • fmt_panel() reuses a recent additional theme in batches, including after the four-theme cache stops scanning, avoiding repeated grid resolution when later plots share a theme.

  • fmt_panel() checks automatically restored grid contrast against the colour of transparent panel fills composited over a known opaque plot background, preserving background transparency and explicit grid colours.

  • fmt_panel() rejects themes, aesthetic mappings and other non-plot gg components instead of returning a theme or silently producing NULL.

  • fmt_panel() corrects matching background colours in automatically restored major, minor and axis-specific grids while preserving explicit plot styles.

  • fmt_his() follows binned position mappings before and after statistics, matching native distribution counts and geometry while preserving original points, axes and unscaled mappings.

  • fmt_his() delegates unscaled distributions without an x scale to native ggplot2 statistics, retaining supported histograms instead of returning empty layers.

  • fmt_his() preserves final after_scale() x mappings without evaluating them again, keeping distribution positions aligned with native layers.

  • fmt_his() normalizes time-difference samples to numeric positions while retaining their units, preventing empty histogram and density overlays.

  • fmt_his() retains the original panel’s resolved x limits when computing distributions, including function, formula and partial limits. Automatic density grids also cover the original scale range, preserving visible tails for externally supplied samples without retraining the original axes.

  • fmt_his() preserves unscaled I() x mappings, preventing repeated transformations and scale-limit censoring of their distribution samples.

  • fmt_his() skips inapplicable layer data when resolving distribution samples, including annotations and data frames missing an explicit variable. Function and formula data retain their deferred evaluation.

  • fmt_his() transforms continuous distribution samples once using each panel’s final x scale, avoiding redundant transformations while retaining original axes and externally supplied samples.

  • fmt_his() rejects unsupported coordinates added after formatting during plot building, with the same clear error as coordinates supplied initially.

  • fmt_his() documents standard facet matching for external data, including repeated samples and newly introduced panels, and adds a deferred-facet example.

  • fmt_his() identifies its own distribution layers without reserving a mapped aesthetic name, preserving unrelated fields with matching names.

  • fmt_his() evaluates each distribution layer’s x mapping once per build and reuses the evaluated values for its statistics.

  • fmt_his() preserves individual facet scales, including scales added after formatting, and avoids applying their position transformations twice.

  • fmt_his() anchors default overlays to the display bottom when Cartesian coordinates reverse the vertical direction.

  • fmt_his() retains distribution layers and their individual settings when a facet is added or replaced after formatting.

  • fmt_his() preserves the plot when a density panel has fewer than two samples or a distribution layer has no finite samples.

  • fmt_his() defers overlay scaling to the normal plot build, avoiding an extra evaluation of original statistics and data callbacks. Overlay heights follow later axis changes and repeated calls keep their individual settings.

  • fmt_his() validates overlay controls and documents their defaults, units, mode-specific effects and supported mappings with runnable simulated examples.

  • fmt_his() resolves layer data and preserves x-mapping expressions and their environments, including .data and .env pronouns.

  • fmt_his() traverses nested patchworks recursively while preserving layouts, annotations, spacers, wrapped grobs and plot-list names.

  • fmt_his() uses independent distribution mappings, avoiding inherited groups, weights and missing aesthetics in externally supplied data.

  • fmt_his() scales each facet independently and keeps distribution layers out of position-scale training, preserving original axes and externally supplied samples.

  • fmt_his() preserves flipped and fixed-ratio Cartesian coordinates and correctly positions overlays on transformed axes without transforming limits twice.

  • fmt_his() anchors histogram and density fills to the requested lower boundary, including negative y ranges and explicit y_rescale intervals.

  • fmt_his() preserves histogram frequency and density ratios when every computed bin or density value is positive, including equally populated bins.

  • fmt_panel() reuses resolved settings for repeated themes within a batch, with a bounded cache that stops after consecutive theme mismatches.

  • fmt_panel() gives automatically restored grids a contrasting grey when their colour matches a known opaque background, preserving explicit grid colours.

  • fmt_panel() uses absolute millimetres for grid and border widths and rejects relative width objects before rendering.

  • fmt_panel() restores hidden grids without fixing inherited styles onto axis-specific elements, so later parent grid themes still take effect.

  • fmt_panel() builds shared panel settings once and avoids redundant plot copies when restoring grid lines.

  • fmt_panel() documents its grid-style fallback, protected cells and extra-theme overrides, with regressions for rendering, computed data and caller-owned plots.

  • fmt_panel() reports malformed border, colour, line-width and line-type arguments before rendering; transparent colours and zero widths remain valid.

  • fmt_panel() formats every ordinary leaf of nested patchworks and lists, preserving container layouts, annotations and list names.

  • fmt_scale() merges deferred argument abbreviations by their matched names in call order, including trans / transform; duplicates within one call remain errors and explicit NULL settings are retained.

  • fmt_panel() restores enabled grids when switching modes or formatting themes that previously hid their grids, retaining available inherited line styling.

  • fmt_panel() consistently hides axis-specific grid lines and applies explicit grid styling to both axes.

  • fmt_scale() uses native scales for statistic-generated axes, including categorical after_stat() values and implicit statistic default mappings.

  • fmt_scale() defers dynamic mapping evaluation to normal plot building, preserving function-call counts, lazy bindings and random-number state.

  • fmt_scale() retains the same observations for partially automatic limits when changing between increasing and decreasing transformations.

  • fmt_expand() leaves lazy mapping bindings unevaluated until plot building, retaining native mapping evaluation order and random-number state.

  • Alternating fmt_expand() and fmt_scale() retains all deferred settings; the most recent formatter takes precedence when both set expansion.

  • fmt_expand() defers active bindings in mapping environments without evaluating them or changing the random-number state during formatting.

  • fmt_expand() retains native scales when axes are supplied by statistic default mappings, including categorical outputs from custom statistics.

  • fmt_scale() preserves observations when changing to or from a reversed transformation, including on the minimum supported ggplot2 version.

  • fmt_scale() formats all leaves of nested patchworks and applies settings to native scales for function and formula layer data without extra data calls.

  • fmt_scale() validates named axis lists, matches unambiguous argument abbreviations consistently, and retains the cause of scale construction errors.

  • fmt_scale() supports controls on existing binned position scales and reuses unchanged scales. Changed axes clone once per plot without retaining prior scale instances or bound callback histories.

  • The formatting vignette uses the current fmt_scale(x = ..., y = ...) API.

  • fmt_expand() retains native scale inference for computed statistics, including categorical after_stat() mappings.

  • fmt_expand() preserves native scale_type() dispatch for extension classes, including implicit binned position scales, without extra dispatch calls.

  • fmt_expand() defers function-call mappings to normal plot building, avoiding extra evaluations and preserving random mappings. Function errors are reported at build time with their original cause.

  • fmt_expand() keeps scale storage bounded when padding changes repeatedly, retaining custom scale classes, fields and clone behavior without chaining previous instances as parents.

  • fmt_expand() and fmt_scale() ignore empty position mappings when choosing a scale, so later non-empty layers retain their native scale type.

  • fmt_expand() retains native scales for function and formula layer data, resolving them during plot building without extra calls to the data function.

  • fmt_expand() and fmt_scale() infer only initial-stage mappings, keeping computed statistics separate from same-named source columns and accepting legacy statistic mappings.

  • fmt_scale() updates only the supplied settings of an existing position scale instead of replacing it, so limits, breaks, labels, transformation, expansion and secondary axes set earlier are kept. Continuous limits use the existing transformation.

  • fmt_expand() reuses unchanged scales and clones changed scales only once per plot, avoiding retained clone histories during repeated formatting.

  • fmt_text() gains axis_titles (default "collect"), passed to patchwork::plot_layout(), so labels shared by all panels of a patchwork are drawn once. Use axis_titles = NULL to keep the previous layout.

  • fmt_expand() reports ordinary mapping errors with their original cause instead of silently substituting a continuous scale. Computed statistics remain deferred to ggplot2.

  • fmt_expand() validates scalar axis choices and finite padding values, with documented scalar/asymmetric expansion and temporal units.

  • fmt_expand() updates every nested patchwork leaf, retaining layouts, annotations, free settings, named containers, spacers and inset overlays.

  • fmt_expand() resolves layer data, mapping overrides and captured variables when choosing new scales. Shared detection also supports fmt_scale().

  • fmt_expand() distinguishes dates, date-times and times, retaining sub-day resolution. Shared detection also accepts temporal controls in fmt_scale().

  • fmt_expand() preserves existing position scales, including transformations, limits, custom labels, discrete ordering, binned scales and secondary axes.

  • fmt_com() limits statistical closures to the current plot’s configuration, so extracting one formatted plot no longer retains other container plots and their data during serialization.

  • fmt_com() validates layout-vector sizes and transformation domains, matches vectors to comparison identities across facet filtering, and supports symmetric or left/right tip lengths per comparison without recycling.

  • fmt_com() fixes one-sided comparison direction to custom pair order, reference order, or original mapped group order for automatic pairs, keeping axis reordering from reversing the tested alternative.

  • fmt_com() preserves paired observations through missing-value and scale filtering, with joint pair omission. method.args$id matches explicit subject IDs; ambiguous unequal-size row pairing is rejected.

  • fmt_com() drops unused comparison levels within each grouped subset, retaining valid sparse legend comparisons and their original dodge positions.

  • fmt_com() retains adjusted P values and labels when grouped subsets have different numbers of comparison levels, respecting group/panel adjustment.

  • fmt_com() honors reference-group comparisons, including pooled references and named legend groups, and rejects conflicting custom comparison lists.

  • flatten_patchwork() rejects unknown, unnamed and duplicate layout controls, reporting misspelled arguments and misplaced extra graphics explicitly. Multiple graphics remain supported through the plots list input.

  • flatten_patchwork() binds insets before extracting hosts from plain or nested lists, retaining composite and grob hosts, their cell names and selection boundaries consistently with native patchwork inputs.

  • flatten_patchwork() emits ordinary inset hosts at the same layout level as their neighbours, retaining shared axis and axis-title collection. Selection and reordering still operate on complete host/inset cells; returned patchwork child indexing now includes inset objects. Composite inset hosts stay intact.

  • fmt_com() validates comparisons, numeric positions and test-option names; resolves unambiguous layer data/mappings and explicit statistical overrides; and skips missing panel pairs without failed-test warnings. Retained unused axis categories no longer compress ordinary or grouped bracket positions.

  • fmt_com() transforms absolute bracket positions from data units and resolves proportional positions within each panel’s trained y range. Explicit positions no longer receive an implicit nudge; a supplied bracket nudge remains supported.

  • fmt_com() formats all ordinary leaves of nested patchworks and plot lists, retaining layout, annotations and names while skipping spacers, guide areas, insets and frozen wrapped graphics.

  • fmt_com() supports pair selection for Dunn, Tukey and Games-Howell tests without passing unsupported comparison arguments. Their full-family adjustment is retained; adjusted-only methods display adjusted stars.

  • fmt_com() honors explicit grouped comparisons and statistical mappings, resolving requested pairs within each subset and retaining native dodge positions. Default trajectory grouping remains ignored for x comparisons.

  • fmt_com() merges named ggpubr arguments with defaults, allowing paired and one-sided test options, custom significance symbols and font overrides without duplicate arguments. Pair selection remains controlled by com_method.

  • fmt_com() accepts adjusted P-value labels and custom ggpubr templates while retaining its default raw P-value stars.

  • fmt_com() resolves comparisons from observed groups and trained axis positions, preventing missing factor levels from silently selecting another group. Consecutive and all-pairs comparisons respect panel-local scale order.

  • flatten_patchwork() documents collection scope changes after flattening, multiple guide-area behavior, and wrapped groups for retaining nested scopes. Examples cover composite inset hosts and protected guide groups.

  • flatten_patchwork() rejects duplicate cell names when a character design would merge them, preventing silent loss of repeated selections. Unnamed lists retain positional repetition in character designs.

  • flatten_patchwork() keeps cell names through nested lists without adding container-name prefixes, including named plots with insets in character layout designs.

  • flatten_patchwork() groups insets with their host before recursion, retaining a composite host as one selectable cell and preserving inset coordinates relative to that entire host.

  • flatten_patchwork() distinguishes a freed plot from its enclosing patchwork, allowing containers ending in free() leaves to flatten, render and retain their overall annotations and collection settings.

  • flatten_patchwork() reports the index and original cause of unreadable patchwork children instead of silently removing them from the result.

  • flatten_patchwork() preserves top-level annotations and collection settings, accepts explicit layout overrides and keeps free() containers intact. Grid geometry is rebuilt from the requested output layout.

  • flatten_patchwork() retains nested insets with their main plot during flattening, selection and reordering, preserving overlay placement.

  • flatten_patchwork() validates selection and row-interleaving indices before arranging plots, preventing fractional-index omissions and empty output. Integer exclusion, repetition and zero indices retain their existing meaning.

  • flatten_patchwork() accepts single plots and nested lists, retaining names for named layout designs and rejecting invalid list elements.

  • fmt_legend() reuses unchanged guide layouts and keeps a stable container parent for layout updates, preventing accumulated wrappers during repeated formatting while retaining later native guide edits.

  • fmt_legend() scales inherited legend text and title margins, leaving other plot text unchanged and retaining automatic margin adaptation.

  • fmt_legend() collects guides normally when inside plots only use I() mappings without explicit scale limits, retaining real guides and layer mapping overrides without evaluating data callbacks.

  • fmt_legend() preserves inside legends generated by fixed aesthetics, explicit scale limits and forced layer legend display during collection.

  • fmt_legend() retains key-size inheritance when resizing width or height, respecting local guide sizes, relative dimensions and colour-bar direction.

  • fmt_legend() composes existing glyph factors when a scaled guide is reused, preventing recursive guide callbacks while retaining layout and data.

  • fmt_legend() treats size factors of one as unchanged, returning the exact input for neutral-only calls and avoiding accumulated guide clones. Mixed calls still apply their other formatting controls and validate inputs.

  • fmt_legend() includes explicit legend, box, text and title margins in overall scaling, including local guides and collected guide boxes. Automatic text margins remain adaptive, and independent key sizing leaves margins alone.

  • fmt_legend() scales spacing in collected guide boxes at each patchwork level, including existing annotation themes, without rescaling legend keys.

  • fmt_legend() checks visible guides within each collection scope, respecting nested keep layouts, explicit guide positions and disabled guides instead of cancelling unrelated outer guide collection.

  • fmt_legend() retains automatic local guide dimensions and text margins, allowing scaled colour bars and legends to adapt when their position changes.

  • fmt_legend() respects later explicit guide layout definitions from guides() and scales while retaining deferred layout for default guides.

  • fmt_legend() scales legend glyphs with both ggplot2 3.5 and current guide callbacks, passing the theme only when the native method supports it.

  • fmt_legend() leaves explicit axis guides unchanged when positioning, styling or resizing legends, preventing misplaced axes and scaling errors.

  • fmt_legend() validates controls for empty lists, spacers, guide areas and wrapped graphics before returning containers without editable data plots.

  • fmt_legend() recognizes aesthetics renamed by ggnewscale, updating titles and guide styling across multiple colour and fill scales. ggnewscale is an optional suggested package used for compatibility tests.

  • fmt_legend() scales explicit global key spacing in both directions, matching guide-local spacing without changing native inherited defaults.

  • fmt_legend() hides explicit guides through the plot position without discarding their type, titles or settings, allowing later position changes to restore them while keeping intentionally disabled guides hidden.

  • fmt_legend() isolates guide and scale inheritance environments from working plots and avoids cloning empty guide containers for theme-only formatting, preventing excessive serialized-object growth after repeated calls.

  • fmt_legend() warns and keeps subplot guides when requested or existing collection layouts contain inside legends, preventing their silent loss.

  • fmt_legend() resolves local guide dimensions from the guide’s own position, retaining horizontal colour bars and legend title margins when scaling by one.

  • fmt_legend() returns the original object for calls with no formatting controls, retaining container validation while avoiding recursive traversal, theme construction and guide cloning.

  • fmt_legend() collects guides for a single plot with a guide area, warns when collection is requested for a list while retaining its return type, and synchronizes styling in existing nested collection layouts without replacing layouts, annotations or free settings. Identical guides are deduplicated; different guides remain separate.

  • fmt_legend() validates positions, directions, themes, titles, collection flags, scaling factors and layout dimensions before editing plots. Numeric positions and corner shortcuts use the current inside-position theme interface.

  • fmt_legend() merges local guide styling and retains guide order, reversal and aesthetic overrides when combining controls. Legend glyph sizes scale after native key construction, preserving mapped sizes and repeated scaling while leaving plotted data and caller-owned guide objects unchanged.

  • fmt_legend() scales each subplot from its own theme after applying new legend styling, retaining blank text and title elements and collected-guide scaling rather than copying the first subplot’s sizes.

  • fmt_legend() multiplies existing legend units and spacing without converting them to lines. A scale of one retains the rendered legend size; independent width and height factors combine with the overall scaling factor.

  • fmt_legend() retains continuous colour bars, binned colour steps and disabled guides when resizing or arranging legends, and defers guide resolution until normal plot building without evaluating layer data during formatting.

  • fmt_legend() renames default and layer-mapped legend titles, including explicit guide titles, without modifying shared input scales or guides.

  • fmt_bg() clips its background stripes to the panel when coordinate clipping is disabled, preserving foreground annotations outside the panel.

  • fmt_bg() respects explicit discrete position scales when layers supply numeric mapped or fixed positions, including flipped coordinates.

  • fmt_bg() checks complete named manual colours against displayed scale categories, allowing unused data categories to be excluded by scale limits without resolving an unnecessary palette.

  • fmt_bg() draws missing-category stripes in free-scale panels containing only missing values when other panels have valid categories, while plots with no non-missing categories still draw no background.

  • fmt_bg() background methods retain only axis and colour settings, preventing old plot objects from accumulating in closures and serialized plots after repeated formatting.

  • fmt_bg() resolves one category colour map for all panels and data layers, keeping unnamed and palette colours consistent across free-scale facets.

  • fmt_bg() defers mapping expressions and data callbacks to ggplot, supporting after_stat() categories without changing random draws or executing callbacks twice. Axis and palette checks for deferred mappings occur during drawing.

  • fmt_bg() reads layer data generated by functions and formulas and selects categorical data mappings past numeric annotation layers.

  • fmt_bg() uses trained layout scales when drawing polar sectors and radial bands, fixing rendering failures with coord_polar() and coord_radial().

  • plt_sankey() adds label_args$lineheight to control multiline label spacing for boxed and plain text. The default 1.2 preserves the existing appearance.

  • fmt_bg() validates opacity, returns empty or entirely missing categories unchanged, and skips background construction when alpha = 0.

  • fmt_bg() replaces its own background layer on repeated calls, retaining other layers and avoiding accumulated transparency. New colors and opacity update the existing background without modifying the input plot.

  • fmt_bg() formats every data plot in nested patchworks and lists while retaining layouts, annotations, names and freed alignment. Spacers, guide areas, fixed wrapped graphics and inset overlays are left unchanged.

  • plt_sankey() groups styling in flow_args, node_args and label_args. This replaces the old top-level alpha, width, space, label_size and label_hjust arguments; migrate them to the corresponding list fields. It also supports label thresholds, plain text, percentage precision, show_text = "none", custom themes and PDF output through save.

  • fmt_bg() creates background bounds after position-scale transformations, retaining stripes on log-scaled axes without warnings from infinite bounds.

  • fmt_bg() supports facet expressions and marginal panels, binds stripe colors during panel drawing, and retains the original fill scales and legends. It no longer expands all categories across the raw facet combinations.

  • fmt_bg() aligns stripes with trained category positions, scale limits, unused and missing categories, free-scale facets, and flipped coordinates. Background rectangles no longer expand the original panel ranges.

  • plt_sankey() keeps labels centered on their nodes when changing node spacing.

  • fmt_bg() supports character and logical categories, mapping expressions, and data and mappings supplied directly to a layer. Continuous axes are skipped with an informative warning.

  • plt_sankey() keeps nodes distinct across variables even when their labels match, and retains node colours when changing label styles.

  • fmt_bg() honors manual colors without requiring plotthis, retains its default rainbow palette, and reports invalid colors and palette errors.

  • plt_sankey() accepts named vars vectors mapping column names to axis labels, including line breaks. Unnamed vectors retain their existing behavior.

  • fmt_axisTile() preserves native axis decorations when transforming category boundaries, including with ggplot2 3.5.0.

  • fmt_axisTile() makes panel-relative color strips follow their axis guides during patchwork axis collection. Different palettes retain separate guides, including color-only strips without text labels.

  • fmt_axisText() retains rich text inherited from the global theme, including side-specific elements, guide formatting and repeated rotations. Complete plot themes retain precedence, and the global theme is not modified.

  • fmt_axisText() retains plot-level rich text when updating guide rotations or local guide themes, including guides configured on scales. Inherited text properties, relative sizes and caller-owned guides are preserved.

  • fmt_axisTile() preserves rich-text axis element classes and layout settings, avoiding incompatible element merges. Text-mode colors follow each rich label’s axis position rather than its internal text fragment coordinates.

  • fmt_axisTile() help uses self-contained simulated examples and explains scale labels, physical axis selection, facets, nested containers and repeated calls. Other guide kinds retain their original plots instead of being replaced with a standard axis guide. Native guides avoid constructing a separate tile plot for every leaf; text colors use direct position matching, and later relative text sizes are resolved once.

  • fmt_axisTile() respects physical axis sides, retains scale-guide controls after coordinate flipping, leaves disabled guides and continuous labels intact, uses non-empty layer data even with an empty global data frame, and reports unsupported non-Cartesian coordinates explicitly.

  • fmt_axisTile() visits editable leaves in nested patchworks and named lists, retains layouts, annotations, freed alignment, fixed graphics and insets, and supports repeated calls and switching modes without nesting tile strips.

  • fmt_axisTile() colors trained axis values instead of raw data levels, respecting scale order, breaks, display labels, unused levels and NA values. Both modes use axis guides, retain axis titles and defer data/statistic evaluation until drawing. Text mode no longer uses vectorized theme elements. Tile thickness retains its main-panel proportions, and the existing patchwork/list return types are retained. The guide API requires ggplot2 >= 3.5.0.

  • fmt_axisText() returns its validated input unchanged for empty calls and avoids repeated empty-theme construction and element-tree lookups. Explicit additional theme fields retain precedence. Help and examples cover the updated behavior.

  • fmt_axisText() validates scalar angles, justification, sizes, colors and font faces immediately with argument-specific errors. Relative sizes, transparent colors and justification outside 0–1 remain supported.

  • fmt_axisText() computes automatic justification for each Cartesian axis side, handles full turns consistently and retains explicitly supplied justification.

  • fmt_axisText() retains existing text element classes, including rich text, custom properties and blank parents, without reapplying relative font sizes.

  • fmt_axisText() applies formatting through plot, scale and secondary-axis guides, including flipped and radial coordinates. Other guide settings and original objects are retained; justification alone keeps existing guide angles.

  • fmt_axisText() updates explicitly styled primary, secondary and radial axis text elements while retaining blank sides and unrelated element properties.

  • fmt_axisText() visits every data plot in nested patchworks and lists while retaining layouts, annotations, names, freed alignment and inset overlays.

  • fmt_axisText() applies explicit horizontal and vertical justification without requiring a rotation angle, retaining the existing angle and other styling.

  • fmt_axisTile() validates named color maps and scalar styling arguments, uses the intended fallback colors for missing categories, honors show_text in both modes, and leaves empty data plots unchanged.

  • plt_sankey() supports show_text = "all_wrap" to place the node name on the first line and the count and percentage together on the second line. The default "all" and existing label styles retain their single-line output.

  • fmt_axis() hides explicitly styled radial text, major/minor ticks and tick lengths, including local guides and secondary axes. In radial plots, x.axis selects theta and y.axis selects r, following ggplot2 theme inheritance for either theta-variable mapping while retaining axis lines and plotted data.

  • fmt_axis() also hides elements styled by guide-local themes in guides(), position scales and secondary axes. Other guide settings, unselected axes, legends and the caller’s original guide objects are retained.

  • Automatic fmt_axis() selection on lists retains spacer, guide-area and fixed-graphic cells, as well as nested container layouts. Inferred dimensions and capacity checks use the list’s top-level grid entries.

  • fmt_axis() help and formatting examples explain single-plot hiding, recursive indices, layout precedence, secondary axes, fixed graphics and scale-sharing limits. The vignette now uses x.axis = TRUE to hide a single x-axis.

  • Recursive formatters exclude inset overlays containing patchworks from the editable plot count. Axis indices and automatic layout selection address only the main grid, and inset axes remain intact.

  • fmt_axis() constructs only requested axis themes and merges x/y hiding before modifying each selected plot once. Combined and separate axis calls retain the same rendered pixels.

  • fmt_axis() returns unchanged inputs after validation when no axes are selected, avoiding recursive extraction, reconstruction and unused themes. Container types, names, deferred data evaluation and RNG state are retained.

  • plot_dims consistently gives layout-based axis selection precedence over both manual selectors, including one-row, one-column and single-plot layouts.

  • fmt_axis() validates logical selectors and integer plot indices, rejects missing, fractional and out-of-range indices, and applies duplicate indices only once. Empty numeric selections and NULL retain the current axes.

  • fmt_axis() rejects invalid or undersized layout dimensions with explicit errors. Empty trailing rows retain the last occupied row’s x-axes.

  • Automatic fmt_axis() selection follows patchwork cell positions, including column-major grids, spacers, guide areas, nested layouts and spanning designs. Existing layouts and annotations are retained and insets do not occupy cells.

  • fmt_axis() hides explicitly styled axis sides and secondary axes, including minor ticks where supported by ggplot2, without changing the plotted data.

  • fmt_tag() warns when the input already has automatic patchwork tag levels. User-owned automatic and manual tags are retained, while repeated calls still replace only fmt_tag() labels.

  • Missing fmt_tag() colours are consistently transparent in both placement modes, including untyped NA and mixed numeric palette vectors. Infinite palette indices fail during argument validation.

  • fmt_tag() checks evaluated compound padding and radius units, rejecting negative or non-finite lengths before drawing while retaining valid unit arithmetic and restoring the caller’s graphics devices.

  • fmt_tag() skips fixed wrapped graphics with a warning, so invisible labels do not consume the numbering of editable data plots.

  • Retagging plots retains patchwork’s freed alignment settings, including switches between inside and outside labels.

  • Inside fmt_tag() positions remain fixed in displayed panel coordinates under flipped and non-linear coordinates, including free-scale facets.

  • Outside fmt_tag() labels compose with axis, legend, reference-line and strip formatting. Formatters visit data-plot leaves and skip label insets while retaining nested layouts and annotations.

  • fmt_tag() and fmt_plot() help and formatting tutorials now document the supported arguments, replacement and facet behaviour with runnable examples. Regression tests cover rendered labels, nested containers, padding, validation, RNG preservation and deferred data evaluation.

  • fmt_tag() continues automatic lettering after Z as AA, AB and so on, and rejects blank labels, invalid NPC positions, colours, font faces, sizes and padding units before drawing. Custom label recycling remains supported.

  • Repeated fmt_tag() calls replace only their own labels, including switches between inside and outside placement, while retaining user annotations and insets. Label insets do not receive patchwork’s automatic tags. fmt_plot() gives fmt_tag_list precedence over tag_levels with a warning.

  • fmt_tag() accepts one, two or four padding units in both placement modes. Outside boxes honour asymmetric padding and font-relative units, and a zero border width removes the border consistently.

  • fmt_tag() labels all leaf plots in nested containers in order, preserving layouts, annotations and list names. Spacers, guide areas and insets do not consume labels; containers without data plots are returned unchanged.

  • fmt_tag() draws a single inside label per panel with four-sided padding, avoiding duplicated text and repeated alpha blending of label backgrounds.

  • fmt_strip() retains the inherited text face with label_color = NULL even when an explicit or transparent strip fill is supplied.

  • Strip formatters reject frozen wrap_elements() panels explicitly instead of silently losing or retaining strips. Format the original ggplot before wrapping; inset overlays remain outside the formatting grid.

  • fmt_strip2() inherits ggh4x themed strips’ text sizes, angles and colours, including hidden strips and repeated calls. Explicit colours retain precedence.

  • Reapplying fmt_strip(strip = FALSE) or label-free fmt_strip2() hides native strips after theme changes, retaining the saved restoration settings.

  • fmt_strip2() excludes insets from grid dimensions and header positions, preserving user insets and outside fmt_tag() labels in nested containers.

  • fmt_strip2() retains native single-panel facets’ shrink setting, preserving raw-data scale ranges when their headers are replaced.

  • fmt_strip() preserves custom row/column labellers, other variables’ mappings and combined single-line labels when replacing the first facet variable. Repeated relabelling reuses the original labeller rather than stacking wrappers.

  • fmt_strip2() help now uses lightweight self-contained examples and documents supported grids, unchanged data, transparent colours and facet restrictions. Regression coverage includes real rendered headers, RNG state and data/statistic call counts in addition to palette checks.

  • fmt_strip2() treats NA strip colours as transparent, generates palettes only for displayed header directions, and reuses identical palettes within a call. Calls without labels skip layout and palette work when hiding strips.

  • fmt_strip2() validates positive integer grid dimensions, non-empty character labels, R colour specifications and one/two palette names before rendering, reporting the responsible argument instead of low-level graphics errors.

  • fmt_strip2() restores strip settings hidden by fmt_strip() and draws new headers through blank strip themes without losing existing text sizes or angles. Explicit header colours still take precedence.

  • fmt_strip2() handles aligned nested rectangular grids and preserves their layouts and annotations. Spacers and guide areas retain their grid positions without receiving facets; non-aligned nested grids are rejected explicitly.

  • fmt_strip2() follows patchwork’s default grid dimensions and column-wise filling, labels the last occupied panel in incomplete rows, and rejects conflicting column counts or unsupported custom designs.

  • fmt_strip2() uses constant header expressions without writing .top. or .right. columns, supporting empty plots, layer-only and function-valued data while preserving existing mappings and computed layer values.

  • fmt_strip2() keeps native facet panels and statistics when hiding their strips, and rejects replacing multi-panel native facets before statistics are computed instead of silently combining data panels.

  • fmt_strip() validates non-empty character labels and R colour specifications before rendering, while retaining transparent fills, numeric palette colours and ignored styling arguments when hiding strips. Help now explains facet label order, inherited fills, nested containers and hide/show behaviour.

  • fmt_raster(method = "image") renders the whole plot, text included, into one raster image of the given width/height (or the open device’s size). The other backends keep text as vectors, so a text-heavy figure such as a forest-plot table gained nothing from them; as an image it redraws in the RStudio Plots pane about 8x faster. It is meant for on-screen previews, not for publication export.

  • fmt_strip(strip = FALSE) no longer builds plots or executes layer data functions and statistics. Only synthetic facets created by fmt_strip() are dropped; native facets, including currently single-panel facets, retain their structure and support later data changes with strips hidden.

  • fmt_strip(strip = TRUE) restores strips hidden by an earlier call. Explicit colours override leaf theme and ggh4x strip elements without resetting text size or angle; label_color = NULL consistently inherits existing colours.

  • fmt_strip() labels all leaf plots in nested patchworks in order, skipping spacers and guide areas without consuming their labels. Nested layouts, annotations and named list containers are preserved.

  • fmt_strip() adds synthetic strips with a constant facet expression instead of overwriting a data column. Empty data, layer-only data and annotations are supported, and existing .strip_label. mappings remain unchanged.

  • fmt_strip() relabels named and computed facet expressions, supports function-valued layer data, and can be reapplied without parsing facet calls as variable names. Other facet variables retain their original labeller.

  • fmt_strip() keeps the complete label vector for a single faceted plot and recycles it across facet levels instead of repeating only its first label.

  • fmt_strip() preserves all facet variables, layout settings and extension classes when relabelling existing facets, keeping panel membership and computed statistics unchanged.

  • fmt_raster() help now distinguishes deferred layer rasterization from immediate fixed-layout capture, documents complete output sizes and list returns, and guards examples with their optional dependencies.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ragg") sets child names when rebuilding panels so captured geometry and retained text are actually drawn in the returned plot.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ragg") captures native raster buffers in memory, avoiding temporary PNG encoding, disk I/O and decoding. This backend no longer requires the png package.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ragg") detects text from grob classes and descendants, including custom names and mixed trees. Viewport geometry no longer bypasses rasterization merely because it has its own viewport.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ragg") rejects conflicting dimensions in shared facet rows/columns and incompatible nested dimensions instead of overwriting earlier panel sizes. Automatic nested outputs retain their complete size.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ragg") resolves automatic panel dimensions from the current device’s grid layout, retaining physical units, free-facet spacing and fixed aspect ratios instead of falling back to a literal size of 4.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ragg") accepts named lists of plots, returns a corresponding list of wrapped gtables, and checks all elements before drawing.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ggrastr") now rasterizes non-text line, polygon, column and other geom layers as well as points and tiles. Text, label and custom annotation layers remain vectors.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ggrastr") recursively rasterizes every leaf plot in nested patchworks while retaining their original layout.

  • fmt_raster() preserves unclipped geometry outside panels by retaining these panels as vectors and reporting the rasterization fallback.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ragg") restores the active graphics device and closes its own devices after both successful rendering and draw errors. Conversion uses a private in-memory device for measurement.

  • fmt_raster() rejects non-positive, non-finite and non-scalar resolutions before opening a raster device. The ragg backend also checks positive finite panel dimensions and rejects dimensions smaller than one output pixel.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ragg") retains the original draw order between vector text and contiguous rasterized geometry runs.

  • fmt_raster(method = "ragg") now preserves all panels, axes and labels in flat and nested patchworks instead of converting only the last plot.

UtilsR 0.6.2

  • fmt_tag() outside placements ("tl-out", "tr-out", "bl-out", "br-out") now draw the label in the same box as inside placements, styled by label.size, label.padding and label.r. The label is a full-plot patchwork inset instead of a ggplot2 tag, so a single ggplot comes back as a single-plot patchwork.

  • stat_ci_parse(exp = "auto") no longer reads a narrow ratio near 1 as a difference. "0.98 (0.95, 1.01)" gave p = 0 because rounding hid the log shape. Scale detection now allows for the printed digits. An interval that cannot be decided follows the decided intervals in x, and is read as a ratio with a warning otherwise. Intervals that are asymmetric on their scale get a warning; their p-value comes from the half facing the null, and level rescales each half (level = 0.95 is now an identity). An estimate outside its bounds, zero width, or a bound <= 0 under exp = TRUE now gives NA with a warning instead of a spurious p-value. Symmetric intervals with an explicit exp give the same results as before.

  • stat_ci_parse() parses the whole vector at once (about 10x faster) and reads more spellings: ;, ~ and em dash separators, a negative upper bound after a hyphen ("-0.50 (-0.80--0.20)"), leading +, exponents, full-width punctuation and the Unicode minus. NA and "" no longer warn. Text after the closing bracket is dropped with a warning instead of silently. stat_ci() shares the parser.

  • stat_ci_parse() output fixes: output = "ci_p" writes p<0.001 instead of p=<0.001; a bound that rounds to zero prints 0.00, not -0.00; decimals follow the most precise of the three numbers, so "1.2 (0.95, 1.59)" is no longer rounded to "1.2 (0.9, 1.6)" and integers stay integers (at least one decimal with level, as before); names of x are kept; character(0) returns an empty character or numeric vector. An estimate equal to the null on a printed bound gets p = 1 instead of NaN. level, digits and map_signif are checked up front with a clear error. stat_ci() shares the decimal rule.

  • stat_ci_parse(output = "p") no longer returns exactly 0 for a very strong effect: "5.00 (4.00, 6.25)" gave 0 and now gives 2.3e-45, so -log10(p) stays finite. The two-sided tail is 2 * pnorm(-|z|); other p-values move by at most 1e-16 and no formatted output changes.

  • stat_ci_parse() and stat_ci() read an en or em dash written as a minus sign, as Word and PDF tables often print it: "–0.25 (–0.40, –0.10)" failed to parse and now equals "-0.25 (-0.40, -0.10)". A dash counts as a minus only before a number that opens the string or follows the bracket or a separator, so "0.25 (0.10–0.40)" keeps it as the separator.

  • ggprism moved from Suggests to Imports: theme_my() reads its palette from ggprism, so theme_my(), theme_km, theme_rcs and theme_scatter no longer fail or stay NULL when ggprism is not installed.

  • Added plt_alluvial() for percentage or count alluvial distributions with native faceting and grouped flow, stratum, label, facet, and legend options; plt_dist(type = "alluvial") now uses it and supports facet without scMMR. Its five semantic list arguments now expose complete defaults in the public signature, with every supported child field documented individually.

  • pal_show_brewer() and pal_show_hcl() now display RColorBrewer and base R HCL palette collections through pal_show().

  • pal_show_hcl() now handles HCL palettes outside the three named type groups when displaying the complete palette collection.

  • Added pal_show_ggsci() and pal_show_viridis() for displaying dynamic ggsci and viridis palette collections through pal_show().

  • pal_show_ggsci() and pal_show_viridis() now support output = "console" consistently with pal_show().

  • pal_show(), pal_show_brewer(), and pal_show_hcl() now support output = "console" through show_color().

  • pal_show() now gives the Colours column a fixed width of 420px in gt output.

  • pal_show() now doubles the width of each colour swatch in gt output.

  • show_color() now prints a dput() representation of the displayed colour vector for reuse in R.

  • .cat_line(), .cat_box(), .cat_message(), .cat_formula(), and .cat_tb() are now exported for use by other R packages.

  • fmt_strip() now centers strip text horizontally and vertically.

  • fmt_strip() gains strip. strip = FALSE removes every strip, including strips already on the plot; multi-panel facets keep their panels.

  • theme_my() now centers horizontal and vertical facet-strip text with symmetric margins.

  • fmt_strip2() now accepts top_right_fill to generate get_facet-style sequential colour fills for top and right strips.

  • fmt_strip2() now defaults top_right_fill to c("Grays", "Greens").

  • fmt_strip2() now uses a lighter second strip colour when a palette is mapped to exactly two levels.

  • impute_na_knn() adds weighted K-nearest-neighbour imputation for mixed data frames while preserving numeric and character value labels.

  • plt_na() adds missing-value matrix and percentage plots; output selects either combined layout or either standalone panel, and sort controls variable ordering by missing rate.

  • plt_upset() now documents levels = NA for plotting missing-value intersections without modifying the input data.

UtilsR 0.6.1

Patch release fixing fmt_strip() re-application failure.

Bug fixes

  • fmt_strip() previously crashed with Error: Can't convert a call to a string. when applied to a plot whose first fmt_strip() pass had injected a synthetic .strip_label. facet. This happened because the no-facet branch wrote the facet quosure as vars(.data[["..."]]) (a CALL), and the has-facet branch used rlang::as_name() which only accepts symbols.

    Two-layer fix:

    1. Source side (no-facet branch): use rlang::sym(".strip_label.") to produce a bare symbol, so subsequent rlang::as_name() calls resolve cleanly.
    2. Recovery side (has-facet branch): add a tolerant .extract_var_name() helper that tries as_name() first, falls back to parsing .data[[...]] calls (for backward compatibility with externally-built ggh4x facets), and drops unparseable entries.

    Reproducer: any patchwork composition where each sub-plot was passed through fmt_strip() once before being wrapped, then fmt_strip() is applied to the wrapped patchwork (e.g. MLR’s .plt_vd.cat.group_sur and .plt_vd.cat.group helpers).

    No public API change; behavior preserved for single-pass fmt_strip() usage. Fix verified end-to-end in MLR (plt_vpd_log cat-cat 2var path which previously crashed now passes).

UtilsR 0.6.0

New: fct_to_group()

  • Companion to fct_to_combine(). Collapses factor levels into new groups specified by integer indices, with auto-naming convention g<i1>/<i2>/... (common in clinical TNM / RPA staging).

  • Vector API (no data parameter), parameter named g_lis:

    x <- factor(c("I","II","III","IV","V"))
fct_to_group(x, list(c(1,3), c(2,4), 5))             # -> g1/3, g2/4, g5
fct_to_group(x, list(early = 1:2, late = 3:5))       # user names win

Breaking Change: fct_to_combine() signature

  • Removed the data parameter. The function now takes vectors directly via ..., aligning with forcats::fct_cross() and base::interaction().

  • Migration:

    # Before (0.5.x and earlier)
fct_to_combine(df, sex, age)
fct_to_combine(df, c("sex", "age"))

# After (0.6.0+)
fct_to_combine(df$sex, df$age)
df %>% mutate(g = fct_to_combine(sex, age))           # natural in mutate
do.call(fct_to_combine, df[c("sex", "age")])           # programmatic
rlang::exec(fct_to_combine, !!!df[c("sex", "age")])    # programmatic (rlang)

  • Default separator (&) and factor-level-ordered output unchanged.

UtilsR 0.3.0

plt_cat() — Unified Categorical Plot

  • Single entry point for 11 chart types: bar, rose, ring, pie, trend, area, dot, sankey, chord, venn, and upset.
  • 27+ parameters: grouping, splitting, dodge/stack, labels, background bands, NA handling, and more.
  • UpSet: switched from ggVennDiagram(force_upset) to ggupset::scale_x_upset().
  • Labels: switched from geom_text to ggrepel::geom_text_repel().
  • Ring/Rose: support position = "dodge".

New Parameters

  • subtitle, legend.direction, aspect.ratio — layout control.
  • NA_color, NA_stat — explicit NA handling with configurable colour.
  • keep_empty — preserve empty factor levels.
  • bg.by, bg_palette, bg_alpha — background colour bands in dodge mode.
  • stat_level — specify positive level for venn/upset.
  • facet_ncol, facet_byrow — split panel layout.
  • force — safety check for > 100 levels.

Bug Fixes

  • alpha not passed to bar/rose/trend/pie geom_col().
  • No-group bar stacking at “all” instead of individual bars.
  • Dodge labels using stack position.
  • keep_empty filter logic inverted.
  • Division by zero in percent mode with empty groups.
  • Ring padding row polluting legend.
  • Venn ignoring user palette.
  • Trend mixed discrete/continuous x-axis conflict.
  • Area type not rendering in dodge mode.

Documentation

  • pkgdown site: https://hui950319.github.io/UtilsR/
  • Vignette: plt_cat_guide with all 11 types.
  • Package docs: added Plot Functions section.

UtilsR 0.2.0

New Functions

  • stat_ci() — Build or reformat CI strings and mean(SD). Accepts both numeric and character input.
  • stat_pval() — Format p-values with stars, threshold display, or add stars to any value.
  • stat_ci_parse() — Parse CI strings, auto-detect exp transformation, compute p-values, adjust confidence levels.
  • fct_cat() — Unified factor manipulation: recode, reorder, reverse, binary, group, combine.
  • fct_num() — Numeric to factor via cut points or quantile/equal binning.
  • fmt_plot() — Master ggplot formatting function chaining axis, tag, legend, ref.
  • fmt_axis() — Hide/show axis elements for multi-plot layouts.
  • fmt_tag() — Add panel labels (A, B, C…) to plots.
  • fmt_legend() — Format legend position, direction, merge across patchwork.
  • fmt_ref() — Add reference lines with per-line colors.
  • fmt_strip() — Add coloured facet strip labels.
  • fmt_com() — Add pairwise statistical comparisons via ggpubr.
  • fmt_bg() — Add coloured background stripes.
  • fmt_his() — Add marginal histogram/density overlay.
  • fmt_scale() — Set axis scales with auto-detection.
  • fmt_expand() — Set axis expansion.
  • fmt_boxplot() — Overlay boxplot layer on violin/jitter plots.
  • fmt_point() — Unified point/jitter/beeswarm layer with auto-dodge and white border.
  • flatten_patchwork() — Recursively flatten nested patchwork objects.
  • show_color() — Display colour swatches in RStudio console.
  • as_palette() / pal_list() — Create and browse colour palettes.
  • theme_my() / theme_km() / theme_rcs() / theme_legend1() — ggplot2 themes.

Colour Palettes

  • 11 built-in palettes: pal_lancet, pal_ditto, pal_igv, pal_polychrome, pal_glasbey, pal_alphabet, pal_ucsc, pal_kelly, pal_d3, pal_simpsons, pal_trubetskoy.
  • Auto-display swatches when printing in console via palette S3 class.

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed .detect_scale_type() accessing ggplot_build() data incorrectly — now reads from plot$data directly.
  • Fixed fmt_strip() crash when plot$data is NULL.
  • Removed fragile ggplot2::.pt usage in fmt_tag() — now uses size.unit = "pt".
  • Fixed fmt_point() checking "color" in mapping names (ggplot2 uses "colour").
  • Removed silent expand injection in fmt_scale() that overrode user intent.
  • Fixed fmt_com() label.y default changed to NULL (auto-calculate, not 0.8).

UtilsR 0.1.0

  • Initial release with lv(), na(), check_system(), check_size(), operators, and console display utilities.
